facts.fact: Comores Droit states that the registration of births, marriages, deaths and recognitions has for decades rested on paper registers, often incomplete and hard to keep; it gives no date for the statement, so the published date is used.
facts.system: état civil (registres papier des centres d'état civil)

facts.fact: Comores Droit describes births, marriages and deaths as registered in paper registers, with a digital system (eCRVS) only proposed by the preliminary study; no event is stated as registered digitally, and the published date is used.
facts.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: The preliminary study covered 37 civil-status centres and proposes a pilot phase in three centres (Moroni, Mutsamudu, Fomboni) before expansion to all centres of the three islands and consulates; of the 37, fewer than half have stable electricity, one in five has internet access and nearly 70% need a complete upgrade, as relayed by Comores Droit.
facts.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: A national workshop to validate the preliminary study for the digitalisation of civil registration was held on 25 March 2026, at which the Ministry of the Interior and UNICEF presented the study's conclusions and the proposed eCRVS system.
facts.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: The Ministry of the Interior, with UNICEF, presents the preliminary study and the proposed eCRVS system at the validation workshop of 25 March 2026, according to Comores Droit.
facts.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)

facts.fact: The study concludes that success depends on political will and on mobilising financial resources in the coming months for infrastructure, equipment and training; no source of finance is named.
facts.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)

systems.system: eCRVS (Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics)
